proposal.summary: Multiple DrayTek products use hardcoded encryption keys in firmware allowing attackers to bind affected devices to attacker-controlled accounts, create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses, and synchronize them from the website.
proposal.affected_product: DrayTek Vigor Routers firmware < 3.9.6 / < 4.2.4; Access Points firmware < v1.4.0; Switches firmware < 2.6.7; Myvigor firmware < 2.3.2
proposal.cwe_quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys

AV.quote: attackers to bind any affected device to their own account

PR.quote: attackers to bind any affected device to their own account

C.quote: create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website

I.quote: create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website

A.quote: create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website

proposal.recommended_next_step: Request or obtain proof-of-concept details (requests, logs, or firmware snippets) showing the hardcoded key and the binding/authentication flow; coordinate disclosure with vendor and verify affected versions and remediation steps.
